knowledge_point.title: Finding the Jacobian of a Three-Dimensional Transformation

question.:question/problem:
Find the Jacobian determinant of the transformation $T,$ defined as

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v \\ w\end{bmatrix}⟶\begin{bmatrix}- 3 u + 3 \cos{\left(w \right)} \\ 3 v \\ - 3 w - \cos{\left(u \right)}\end{bmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a transformation 

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v \\ w\end{bmatrix}\to \begin{bmatrix}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{bmatrix},
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & \frac{∂x}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & \frac{∂y}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & \frac{∂z}{∂w}\end{vmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Here, we have 

$$
x(u,v,w)=- 3 u + 3 \cos{\left(w \right)}\, y(u,v,w)=3 v\, z(u,v,w)=- 3 w - \cos{\left(u \right)}.
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & =-3 & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & =0 & \frac{∂x}{∂w} & =- 3 \sin{\left(w \right)} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & =0 & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & =3 & \frac{∂y}{∂w} & =0 \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & =\sin{\left(u \right)} & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & =0, & \frac{∂z}{∂w} & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =\begin{vmatrix}-3 & 0 & - 3 \sin{\left(w \right)} \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ \sin{\left(u \right)} & 0 & -3\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(3\right)(-1)^{2+2}\begin{vmatrix}-3 & - 3 \sin{\left(w \right)} \\ \sin{\left(u \right)} & -3\end{vmatrix} \\  & =9 \sin{\left(u \right)} \sin{\left(w \right)} + 27.\end{aligned}
$$
